mainEntity.name: Will a dentist be able to tell which implant system was used?

acceptedAnswer.text: In some cases, a dentist may be able to identify the implant brand from X-rays, particularly if the design characteristics are recognisable. However, this is not always possible without manufacturer records. If the exact system cannot be confirmed, this will primarily be relevant if prosthetic components (such as the abutment or crown) need replacing in the future. For routine monitoring and hygiene maintenance, the exact brand is not always essential. It is still worth sharing any documentation you have from your original clinic to help the reviewing dentist build as complete a picture as possible.

mainEntity.name: Can another dentist treat a problem with my implant if they didn't place it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in many cases a qualified dentist or implant specialist can manage problems such as peri-implant disease, a loose crown, or soft tissue concerns, even if they were not involved in the original placement. The ability to intervene will depend on the nature of the problem and the individual clinical situation. Some complex cases — particularly those involving the implant fixture itself — may require input from a specialist. Your reviewing dentist will advise you on the most appropriate course of action following examination.

mainEntity.name: How often should a dental implant be checked?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most dental professionals recommend that implants are reviewed at least once per year as part of a routine dental examination. However, the frequency of checks may be higher for patients who have had previous complications, those with a history of gum disease, or those who smoke. Your dentist will recommend a monitoring schedule based on your individual needs and clinical findings. In between formal reviews, professional hygiene appointments are also recommended to maintain the health of the gum tissue around the implant.

mainEntity.name: Is it normal to feel discomfort around a dental implant years after placement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some mild sensitivity during healing is expected in the weeks immediately following implant placement. However, discomfort that develops or persists long after the implant has fully integrated is not considered normal and should be assessed by a dental professional. In many cases, late-onset discomfort around an implant may be related to peri-implant inflammation or an issue with the crown or bite alignment, both of which can often be managed when identified early. It is always advisable to seek a clinical assessment rather than waiting to see whether symptoms resolve on their own.

mainEntity.name: What is peri-implantitis, and should I be concerned about it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Peri-implantitis is an inflammatory condition that affects the gum tissue and bone surrounding a dental implant. It is similar in some respects to periodontitis (gum disease) in natural teeth and can, if left unmanaged, lead to bone loss around the implant. Risk factors include poor oral hygiene, smoking, a history of gum disease, and infrequent professional monitoring. It is not a reason for alarm, particularly when identified at an early stage — but it does highlight the importance of regular implant reviews and professional hygiene support. A dentist can assess whether any signs of peri-implant disease are present and advise accordingly.

mainEntity.name: Can I register with a new dental practice specifically for my implant care?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You are entirely within your rights as a patient to register with a new dental practice for your ongoing care, including implant monitoring. Many patients in London and across the UK do this when they relocate, when their existing clinic closes, or simply when they feel another practice may better suit their needs. When registering, let the practice know that you have a dental implant and request that an implant review is included as part of your initial new-patient examination. You can also request that your records be transferred from your previous clinic where this is possible. If you are ready to arrange this, you can book an appointment online with our London clinic.
